title: Theory of the Spinon-Mediated Witness Spin Glass in Herbertsmithite
abstract: Herbertsmithite is a prototypical candidate quantum spin liquid (QSL), believed to feature a long-range entangled ground state and deconfined fractionalised spinon excitations. Confirmation of these properties has been hindered by the presence of magnetic impurities (spin-1/2 Cu2+ spins substituted onto non-magnetic Zn2+ sites). Recently these impurities were reconceptualised as 'witnesses' of the QSL, inheriting long-range interactions and entanglement mediated by the QSL spinons, leading to spin glass formation amongst witnesses below 260 mK. Here we present a full theoretical account of this idea. Despite having only one free parameter (the witness-kagome spin coupling), our model captures the full range of experimental data, including: the formation of a spin glass amongst witnesses; the frequency and temperature dependence of the magnetic noise; a sharp peak in the DC magnetic susceptibility as a function of temperature; and the static neutron scattering structure factor at 2 K. Both candidate QSLs (Z2 and U(1)) give similar agreement with all data; however, our model predicts a qualitative difference between the Z2 and U(1) neutron scattering intensities below 260 mK, providing a long-sought definitive test to distinguish the two cases. We also predict phase diagrams as a function of temperature and witness concentration, finding a phase transition to different long-range ordered witness states for Z2 and U(1) at high concentration.
summary: This theoretical work models the spin glass behavior in Herbertsmithite, where magnetic impurities interact via spinons from the underlying Quantum Spin Liquid (QSL). By comparing predictions from $\text{Z}_2$ and $\text{U}(1)$ QSL models against multiple experimental measurements, the authors propose a definitive neutron scattering test to distinguish between the two candidate QSL ground states.
main_problem: To provide a full theoretical account of the spin glass formation among magnetic impurities (witnesses) in Herbertsmithite, mediated by the Quantum Spin Liquid (QSL) spinons.
main_result: The model successfully captures multiple experimental signatures, and crucially, predicts a qualitative difference in neutron scattering intensities between the $\text{Z}_2$ and $\text{U}(1)$ QSL candidates, offering a definitive test.
method: The authors developed a theoretical model by deriving an effective witness-witness interaction ($J_{ij}$) from the QSL spinon susceptibility, followed by large-scale classical Monte Carlo simulations.
model_or_system: The system is Herbertsmithite, a prototypical Quantum Spin Liquid (QSL) candidate on a kagome lattice. The model treats magnetic impurities ('witnesses') whose interactions are mediated by the underlying QSL spinons, considering both $\text{Z}_2$ and $\text{U}(1)$ QSL ground states.
key_observables: Spin glass formation temperature ($T^*$), magnetic noise ($S(f, T)$), DC magnetic susceptibility ($\chi(T)$), and static neutron scattering structure factor $S(\mathbf{q})$.
important_parameters: Witness-kagome spin coupling ($\gamma$), temperature ($T$), and witness concentration ($x$).
main_assumptions: Key approximations include treating the witness spins as classical Ising spins and using mean-field theory for the QSL description, neglecting back-action of witnesses on the kagome spins.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the model setup, showing $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ witnesses randomly occupying $\text{Zn}$ sites, and the theoretical predictions for various experimental observables like susceptibility and neutron scattering structure factor.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical problem (spin glass in Herbertsmithite), derives the effective Hamiltonian via QSL susceptibility, applies the model to fit multiple experimental data points, and finally uses the differences between $\text{Z}_2$ and $\text{U}(1)$ predictions to propose a definitive experimental test.
why_interesting: This work bridges the gap between abstract QSL theory and concrete experimental signatures in frustrated magnets, providing a clear, testable prediction (neutron scattering difference) that guides future experimental efforts.

figures.caption: FIG. 1: Schematic illustration of our model. Spin-1/2 Cu2+ ions (grey), termed witnesses, randomly occupy a fraction x of non-magnetic Zn sites (not shown). The quantum spin liquid in the kagome Cu2+ plane (brown) mediates an interaction between these witnesses, leading to their observed spin glass formation below T ∗= 260 mK [22].

FIG. 2: The signs of the hopping parameters used to define the QSLs. Solid lines indicate nearest neighbour hoppings t(1) lm (red positive, blue negative) which ensure π gauge flux through each hexagon (the product of hoppings around a hexagon is −1) and 0 flux through triangles. Dashed lines indicate second-neighbour hoppings t(2) lm used to define the Z2 QSL. The 6-atom unit cell, and basis vectors e1 and e2, are also shown.

FIG. 3: The Brillouin zone corresponding to the unit cell convention in Fig. 2; colours indicate the energy of the lowest-energy dispersing spinon band for the U(1) QSL (see Fig. 4), with Dirac nodes evident at EF . Node locations are gauge dependent, but their separation is gauge invariant and sets the behaviour of Jij.
FIG. 4: Spinon bandstructures along ky for the U(1) QSL (blue) and Z2 QSL (red).

FIG. 5: Tripartite colouring of kagome lattice sites. Witnesses sit above/below triangles and couple to the three closest kagome sites. The induced witness-witness coupling Jij involves a sum over 9 kagome spin-spin susceptibilities: 3 of AA/BB/CC type, 6 of AB/BC/AC type.
